messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — severity P1: repeated GPU OOMs / container restarts observed on pool `gpu-preload-prod-2`. 10+ restarts in 5m, increased latency and 503s for some customers. See: https://console.redwood/incident/2928801023 :rotating_light:

alex: taking lead, paging @ops-oncall. I'll gather quick triage info.

ops-oncall: taking pager. Observed many pods in CrashLoopBackOff. kubectl get pods shows restarts:
```
NAME                                      READY   STATUS             RESTARTS   AGE
inference-preload-0                       0/2     CrashLoopBackOff   12         3m
inference-preload-1                       0/2     CrashLoopBackOff   11         3m
router-5b6c8d9f7b-ztx4v                  1/1     Running            0          2d
```
Logs show repeated allocation failures:
```
E tensorflow: 2026-03-15 09:21:03.123 CUDNN_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED: failed to allocate tensor
E runtime: prefill failed: CUDNN_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED (alloc 16432192)
```

sasha: I'm querying prefill size histogram for the last hour. Looks like a tail of very large prefill requests: ~0.4% > 65k tokens, lots of KV cache pressure.

mike: I can cordon the two most-affected nodes to stop new scheduling while we triage. Before we do that, quick mitigation idea: enforce a PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS env override on the pool to reject >16k prefill requests and fall back to streamed prefill. Would prefer to avoid node drains if we can patch quickly.

alex: agree, throttle long prefill. @deploy-bot can we hotpatch the pool with PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=16384 and reduce prefill concurrency to 1 for now?

deploy-bot: Hotpatch request accepted. Rolling update to pool `gpu-preload-prod-2`: setting PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=16384, PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=1.

ops-oncall: running commands now:
```
# set route override
redwoodctl pools update gpu-preload-prod-2 --env PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=16384 --env PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=1
# scale workers down to 6
redwoodctl pools scale gpu-preload-prod-2 --replicas 6
```

deploy-bot: Hotpatch rolling: 3/6 pods updated... 6/6 pods updated.

ops-oncall: After hotpatch, observed drop in new OOMs, restarts slowed. Current pod state:
```
inference-preload-0   2/2   Running   0   10m
inference-preload-1   2/2   Running   0   8m
```

jess: Support note — Customer ACME reported 503s starting ~09:20 UTC. I created support ticket #SR-20260315-54 and sent a brief status update pointing to this incident. They were impacted for ~7 minutes.

alex: quick customer-impact summary for post-incident: ~23 failed requests total, 3 enterprise customers saw transient 5xx, no data loss. Root-cause hypothesis: prefill memory accounting undercounts KV cache usage for long-context sessions; combined with fragmented allocations from a recent cuDNN kernel selection change caused CUDNN_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED rather than clean rejection.

mike: creating follow-up bug INF-8452: "prefill: kv-cache accounting + allocator cap -> OOM with long prompts". Plan: add strict prefill accounting, cap allocator for prefill phase, and add immediate rejection path for requests above safe token threshold.

sasha: I pushed a quick monitoring query to alert on prefill token tail and pod restart rate. Saved at dashboards/preload/prefill-tail.

ops-oncall: notes for handoff -> log bundle uploaded to https://artifacts.redwood/incident/2928801023/logs.tar.gz. Commands executed and timestamps:
- 09:22 set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=16384 and PREFILL_CONCURRENCY=1
- 09:23 scaled pool to 6 replicas
- 09:28 verified pods stable

incident-bot: Pager update: handoff scheduled to SRE morning shift @ 2928803000.

jess: I'll send a second customer update saying we've applied a mitigation, working on a permanent fix, ETA 48h for code patch and 1 week for full rollout.

mike: follow-up actions (INF-8452, create postmortem):
- add allocator cap for prefill (owner: eng-runtime)
- reject too-large prefill requests in router (owner: eng-platform)
- add integration test that simulates long-kv-cache prefill and ensures failure is graceful (owner: eng-ml)

alex: thanks team. Will open postmortem template and include timeline. Leaving pager to morning SRE. :thumbsup:

support-bot: Support ticket SR-20260315-54 updated: mitigation applied, engineering investigating.

ops-oncall: handing off — logs & actions in the incident doc, will follow up on INF-8452. Leaving pager.

alex: closing thread for now, will file full incident PM with timeline + customer comms.
